findings.title: Device limit bypassed on retry via local cache
findings.body: In tagDeviceUI the local cache entry is set on line 87 with a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{}) BEFORE the CreateOrUpdateDevice DB call. When the device limit is reached and that DB call returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, the cache entry is already populated. Any subsequent request from the same client within the 29-minute cache TTL hits the cache (line 83), returns nil immediately, and Authenticate proceeds — bypassing the limit entirely. The limit is therefore only enforced on the very first request for a given device ID; a single retry lets the user through. To actually enforce it, the cache must only be populated after a successful CreateOrUpdateDevice (or the cache key must encode the limit-reached state). This regression is introduced by the new ErrDeviceLimitReached path: the cache pattern was harmless before because all errors were swallowed.

findings.title: TOCTOU race lets device count exceed the configured limit
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice performs CountDevices and then either updateDevice or an INSERT as two separate, non-atomic steps (lines 109-118 and the switch/INSERT at 120-153). Under concurrent anonymous authentications many goroutines can each observe count < deviceLimit, all proceed to insert, and the resulting count can exceed deviceLimit by the concurrency level. This defeats the stated purpose of the feature — the limit is not a hard cap but only an approximate one, and a burst of legitimate users (or a small attacker) can inflate the table well past it. Wrap the check and write in a single transaction (or use a serializable isolation level / advisory lock) so the limit is enforced atomically.

findings.title: Anonymous authentication now blocks synchronously on TagDevice DB writes
findings.body: Previously TagDevice was called in a goroutine with a 2-minute context timeout, so Anonymous.Authenticate returned after one DB lookup (orgService.GetByName). The new code calls TagDevice synchronously at line 44, which internally runs CountDevices (SELECT COUNT(*)) plus an INSERT/UPDATE on anon_device on every anonymous request. Each anonymous authentication now performs 2-3 DB operations instead of 1, and any DB latency or contention is added to auth latency. For Grafana instances that expose anonymous dashboards to high traffic this is a serious performance and reliability regression. The async pattern should be kept; the limit decision can be propagated via a channel, or the CountDevices check alone can be made synchronous while the write stays async.

findings.title: Device-limit failure surfaces as a bare sentinel error with no HTTP semantics
findings.body: Anonymous.Authenticate returns the raw sentinel var ErrDeviceLimitReached = fmt.Errorf("device limit reached") (defined in anonstore/database.go line 18) at line 46, with no HTTP status code, no machine-readable code, and no user-facing message. The authn framework will propagate this as a generic authentication failure, almost certainly a 500/Internal-Server-Error-like response to the browser. Operators have no signal that the limit is the cause (they will see only generic auth-failure logs), and end users see no indication that they are hitting a configured cap versus a real outage. Wrap the sentinel in a typed error that carries a 429/503 status and a clear message, or convert it in the HTTP layer so the response makes the cause actionable.

findings.title: updateDevice uses device.UpdatedAt as its time reference while CreateOrUpdateDevice uses time.Now()
findings.body: In CreateOrUpdateDevice the 30-day window is built from time.Now().UTC() (line 110), but in updateDevice the WHERE bounds on updated_at are built from device.UpdatedAt.UTC() (lines 80-81). They happen to coincide today because TagDevice constructs the Device with UpdatedAt: time.Now() (impl.go line 141), but the two functions now disagree on what 'now' is. If a future caller passes a Device whose UpdatedAt is anything other than time.Now() (a replay, a clock-skew tolerance, a test fixture, a backfill, or simply a refactor), the updateDevice bounds will silently drift relative to the count window: a device that should be considered 'recent' by CreateOrUpdateDevice can be excluded by updateDevice and vice versa. Capture time.Now() once at the start of CreateOrUpdateDevice and pass it (or device.UpdatedAt derived from it) into updateDevice explicitly.

findings.title: No test exercises the allowed update path of updateDevice at the limit
findings.body: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only verifies that a *new* device ID is rejected when the count has reached the limit. The crucial opposite case — a known device ID re-tags while the limit is reached and must be updated successfully via updateDevice — is not tested. This is the only path that uses updateDevice at all in this PR, and a regression that always returns ErrDeviceLimitReached (e.g., the WHERE bounds drifting to exclude every row, as flagged separately) would not be caught. Add a case with deviceLimit=1 that inserts device X, then calls CreateOrUpdateDevice with the same X again (optionally with a slightly different client_ip/user_agent) and asserts no error and that the row was actually updated.

findings.title: Provider signature changes need a corresponding wire/DI regeneration
findings.body: ProvideAnonymousDeviceService now takes sqlStore db.DB instead of anonstore.AnonStore (impl.go line 36), and ProvideAnonDBStore gained a new deviceLimit int64 parameter (anonstore/database.go line 52). The PR updates every direct caller it shows (impl.go and the *_test.go files) but does not include the wire-generated file(s) (e.g. wire_gen.go / providers.go / inject.go) that Grafana's wire setup regenerates from these provider signatures. Until those are regenerated the build will fail because the old ProvideAnonDBStore(store) and ProvideAnonymousDeviceService(..., anonStore, ...) calls no longer exist. Confirm the wire file is regenerated (or hand-updated) as part of this change; if it is intentionally omitted, the PR description should say so.

findings.title: New auth.anonymous device_limit setting is not documented
findings.body: setting.go adds cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit = anonSection.Key("device_limit").MustInt64(0) under [auth.anonymous] at line 1650, but no documentation file is changed. The PR description itself leaves the 'docs are updated' checklist item unchecked. Operators have no reference for the new key, its default of 0 (= no limit), or its semantics (when the limit is reached, new anonymous device IDs are rejected while known devices can still re-tag). Add the key to the appropriate configuration reference (e.g. docs/sources/administration/configuration.md) and, if this is a notable improvement, link it from the What's New doc per the PR template.
